annotation_description: With Scalding Tarn still in hand and two Brainstorms and two Ponders available, casting Thoughtseize before seeing more cards or playing the fetchland is debatable. The standard Legacy sequencing would be to cast Ponder or Brainstorm first to improve hand quality and potentially find better cards to keep, or at minimum play Scalding Tarn first (to have a shuffle effect available for Brainstorm, and to thin the deck). However, Thoughtseize on turn 1 is a very common and defensible play — getting information and disruption early is valuable, especially when you don't know the opponent's hand. The counterargument is that Ponder first lets you see 3 cards and potentially find a better keep, while Thoughtseize's value doesn't diminish much by waiting one turn. But against fast combo decks, turn 1 Thoughtseize is critical. This is close enough to be debatable.

The opponent's hand contains Endurance, Ignoble Hierarch, Springheart Nantuko, and presumably Gaea's Cradle (a land). Ignoble Hierarch is a mana dork, but the opponent also has Gaea's Cradle which needs creatures to produce mana. Taking the Hierarch does slow their mana development, but Endurance is a powerful flash creature that can disrupt graveyard strategies and serves as a 3/4 reach body. Springheart Nantuko combined with Gaea's Cradle could generate significant token value if the opponent draws lands. However, Endurance is arguably the most impactful card here - it's a 3/4 flash creature with reach that can be cast for free via evoke (exiling a green card), and the Villain's hand is full of cantrips (Brainstorm, Ponder) that could be disrupted. Without other green cards to exile for evoke, Endurance requires 1GG to hard-cast, which is harder without Hierarch. The choice between Hierarch and Springheart Nantuko is the real debate - Nantuko with Gaea's Cradle has enormous snowball potential, creating token copies of creatures when lands enter. Taking Nantuko might have been better as it removes the engine piece that could run away with the game alongside Cradle.

Playing Wasteland as the turn 1 land drop provides only colorless mana, while the player's entire hand requires green mana (Springheart Nantuko costs {1}{G}, Endurance costs {1}{G}{G}). This delays meaningful board development by a full turn.

chosen_display: Wasteland — {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Destroy target nonbasic la... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activating Wasteland to destroy the opponent's Underground Sea when it's already tapped means both players lose their only land. While this denies the opponent mana next turn, Gem3P also loses their only current land. With Gaea's Cradle (which needs creatures to produce mana and there are none), Misty Rainforest, and Forest in hand, Gem3P has land drops but loses tempo by sacrificing Wasteland now rather than using it for mana this turn. Playing Forest or Misty Rainforest first (to have mana available), then potentially Wastelanding later when the opponent plays another nonbasic, could have been stronger. However, the Wasteland play does strand the opponent with no mana at all if they don't have another land, which is a legitimate mana denial strategy. The main concern is that Gem3P could have played a land this turn, tapped Wasteland for colorless, and still had Wasteland available to threaten destruction later, maintaining more flexibility.

Playing a land before casting cantrips loses valuable information. With Ponder available and an untapped Underground Sea, the player should cast Ponder first to see the top 3 cards before deciding which land to play. This is a fundamental Legacy sequencing principle - cantrips before land drops lets you make more informed decisions.

chosen_display: Scalding Tarn — {T}, Pay 1 life, Sacrifice {this}: Search your li... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activating Scalding Tarn before casting Brainstorm is a sequencing error. In Legacy, the standard play is to cast Brainstorm first, then use the fetchland to shuffle away the two unwanted cards put back on top. By fetching first, Villain loses the powerful Brainstorm + fetch shuffle interaction, which is one of the primary reasons Brainstorm is so strong in Legacy. With Brainstorm and two fetches (well, one fetch now), the correct line is Brainstorm first, put two bad cards on top, then fetch to shuffle them away.

Declined to cast Brainstorm before playing land for the turn. With a hand of Brainstorm, Brainstorm, Ponder, Ponder, Swamp, casting Brainstorm before the land drop would let Villain see 3 new cards, potentially find better lands or action, and put back duplicates. While there are no fetchlands to shuffle away the top cards, Ponder can serve that role next turn. Declining loses card selection value.

Put back Underground Sea instead of Swamp on top of library from Brainstorm. Underground Sea is strictly better than Swamp (taps for U or B vs just B), so the worse card (Swamp) should be put back and the better card kept in hand. If drawn later, Underground Sea is always preferable to Swamp.

message: Select a card ORDER to put on the TOP of your library (last one chosen will be topmost)
annotation_description: With an empty opponent board and Barrowgoyf in hand costing 3 mana, the Villain chose to draw Fatal Push (removal) instead of Underground Sea (3rd land). Without a 3rd land, the Villain cannot cast Barrowgoyf on turn 3 to apply pressure. The opponent has no creatures to remove, making Fatal Push less immediately useful. While Brainstorm could theoretically find lands, prioritizing a guaranteed land drop for the powerful Barrowgoyf (which would be ~4/5 with deathtouch and lifelink given graveyard types) seems clearly better.

chosen_display: Misty Rainforest — {T}, Pay 1 life, Sacrifice {this}: Search your li... [Activate]
annotation_description: Fetching Misty Rainforest now wastes a landfall trigger. With Forest in hand and Wasteland already in play, they can play Forest and cast Springheart Nantuko ({1}{G}) this turn using Forest + Wasteland. Then next turn, fetching Misty Rainforest with Springheart Nantuko in play would generate a free 1/1 Insect token from the landfall trigger, and playing Gaea's Cradle would generate another landfall trigger.

Put back Orcish Bowmasters on top of library with Brainstorm instead of keeping it in hand. Bowmasters has flash and is the strongest card available, deployable immediately by cracking Polluted Delta. Putting it back delays access by a turn and loses the flash deployment option during opponent's turn.

Casting Endurance for 3 mana when the opponent is completely tapped out misses the opportunity to deploy Sylvan Safekeeper (1 mana) + Springheart Nantuko (2 mana), which deploys two creatures, sets up the Springheart landfall engine with Gaea's Cradle in hand, and provides Safekeeper protection for both. With opponent tapped out, there's no risk of either being countered. Two creatures also make Gaea's Cradle tap for 2G next turn instead of 1G.

Playing Endurance main phase wastes its flash advantage and ETB graveyard-shuffling ability. The opponent has 8 cards in graveyard including key spells, and Endurance's ETB could be used at a critical moment (e.g., in response to a graveyard-dependent play). More importantly, Sylvan Safekeeper should be deployed first as it protects creatures from removal and enables the Springheart Nantuko + land sacrifice synergy. Playing Safekeeper now and holding Endurance for flash timing would be significantly better. Additionally, Gaea's Cradle should be played before casting creatures to potentially generate more mana with creatures already in play, and Springheart Nantuko is a higher priority play as it generates ongoing value with landfall triggers.

Endurance is resolving, which will put all of Villain's graveyard (8 cards including Brainstorms, Ponders, Snuff Out, etc.) on the bottom of their library. Villain has Daze available (by returning an Underground Sea to hand) to counter Endurance, which would preserve their graveyard and prevent the opponent from getting a 3/4 reach creature. The reasoning about 'meticulously sculpted library' from Brainstorm is misguided - Endurance shuffling the graveyard to the bottom of the library doesn't affect the top cards. More importantly, letting a 3/4 creature resolve when you have a free counter available, while also losing 8 cards worth of graveyard resources, is a significant mistake.

Playing Swamp instead of Underground Sea is slightly suboptimal. The player has two Underground Seas already in play and a Polluted Delta. Playing Underground Sea as the land drop preserves more flexibility (access to blue mana from three lands without needing the Delta), and keeps the Swamp in hand as a potential resource. With Daze in hand, having more Islands in play is relevant - though they already have two Underground Seas. More importantly, if they want to cast Orcish Bowmasters this turn (which costs {1}{B}), either land works. But Underground Sea provides both blue and black mana, giving better flexibility for future turns. The Swamp is a basic that can be fetched with Polluted Delta later if needed, while Underground Sea cannot be fetched as easily (Delta can find it, but it's still better to have the dual in play). Playing the dual land preserves the basic for fetch targets and maximizes mana flexibility.

Cast Orcish Bowmasters during precombat main phase instead of holding it. Bowmasters has flash and is significantly better cast on the opponent's draw step to get both the ETB trigger and the draw trigger (2 damage + potentially a 2/2 Orc Army). Additionally, the land (Underground Sea) should have been played before casting the spell to maximize mana availability and Daze protection.

chosen_display: Polluted Delta — {T}, Pay 1 life, Sacrifice {this}: Search your li... [Activate]
annotation_description: Orcish Bowmasters is on the stack and the opponent has all lands tapped. Daze (returning Underground Sea to hand) would counter it for free since the opponent cannot pay {1}. This prevents both the body and the ETB trigger (1 damage + amass). Fatal Push only kills it after it resolves, allowing the ETB to fire.

Declined to Daze Orcish Bowmasters on the stack, allowing it to resolve and get its ETB trigger (1 damage + 1/1 Orc Army token). Even if Fatal Push can kill the Bowmasters afterward, the opponent still gets the token and the damage, plus the ongoing card-draw punishment trigger fires at least once.

Casting Springheart Nantuko before Sylvan Safekeeper is suboptimal sequencing. Playing Safekeeper first (for G) would give immediate protection for Endurance against Fatal Push, and if the opponent uses countermagic (like Daze) on the cheaper spell, the more impactful Nantuko is preserved. Both creatures can be cast this turn regardless of order thanks to Gaea's Cradle scaling with creature count.

Springheart Nantuko is a very dangerous card that enables explosive token generation with landfall triggers, especially with Gaea's Cradle on board (which produces mana based on creature count). With Endurance already on board and Gaea's Cradle, each land drop creates a token, which makes Cradle tap for more mana, enabling the bestow copy ability to snowball. Daze could have countered Springheart Nantuko for free by bouncing an Island, which is a minimal cost. The opponent has 5 lands including Gaea's Cradle and Endurance - letting Nantuko resolve means any subsequent land drop creates tokens, and with Cradle mana the opponent can potentially pay {1}{G} to copy Endurance repeatedly.

Sylvan Safekeeper is a critical threat that will make all of the opponent's creatures untargetable by sacrificing lands. Once it resolves, the opponent can protect Endurance (a 3/4 with reach) and Springheart Nantuko from Fatal Push and any future removal. Daze could counter it here by returning an Island to hand - the opponent has no untapped lands to pay the {1}. Sylvan Safekeeper is especially dangerous alongside Gaea's Cradle and Springheart Nantuko, as it enables a powerful engine where sacrificing lands triggers landfall when replayed. Letting it resolve for free is a significant mistake.

Fatal Push was cast targeting Endurance (mana value 3), but without Revolt active (no permanent left the battlefield under Villain's control this turn), Fatal Push can only destroy creatures with mana value 2 or less. This means the Fatal Push is completely wasted on Endurance. Even if the Orc Army Token dying in combat would trigger Revolt, that happens during the damage step, after Fatal Push has already resolved.

Targeted Endurance (4/5, mana value 3) with Fatal Push instead of Sylvan Safekeeper (1/1, mana value 1). Endurance requires revolt to be eligible for Fatal Push, and opponent has Sylvan Safekeeper with an untapped Gaea's Cradle available to sacrifice, giving Endurance shroud and causing Fatal Push to fizzle entirely. Even if revolt is active, Sylvan Safekeeper is the more strategically important target as it protects all opponent's creatures from future targeted removal. The opponent is far more likely to sacrifice a land to save a 4/5 than a 1/1.

Casting a second legendary Endurance while one is already on the battlefield means one must be sacrificed to the legend rule. This spends Timmy's last card in hand essentially just to 'untap' Endurance and get a mostly irrelevant ETB graveyard shuffle. Keeping Endurance in hand preserves optionality as a flash surprise blocker or meaningful graveyard hate for later.

Declined to block Orcish Bowmasters (1/1) with Sylvan Safekeeper (1/1). Orcish Bowmasters is one of the most impactful creatures in Legacy, punishing card draws and growing army tokens. Trading it away with a Sylvan Safekeeper would be a favorable exchange, removing a persistent threat for free.

Timmy cast Natural Order without first using Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Underground Seas. Since Natural Order only requires Gaea's Cradle (3G from 3 creatures) + Bayou (1G) = GGGG to cast, Wasteland's mana wasn't needed. Destroying an Underground Sea first would reduce the opponent's ability to counter Natural Order (fewer mana sources to pay for Daze, or cast Force of Will pitching + leaving mana for other interaction).

At 1 life, Polluted Delta cannot be activated (costs 1 life to crack) and has no mana ability, making it a completely dead land. Underground Sea would provide actual mana, which matters for casting Daze (hard cast) or having more resources available.

The player has lethal on board with the opponent at 1 life. Endurance (3/4) and Craterhoof Behemoth (5/5) plus Springheart Nantuko (1/1) are on the battlefield - any attack would deal far more than 1 damage. The opponent has Orcish Bowmasters tapped, so there's essentially no blocker available. Instead of moving to combat and attacking for the win, the player passed/declined to act in precombat main phase, wasting time and giving the opponent potential outs.
